details:
CLPS Explorer is an interactive web platform created to make NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program easier to understand and explore.

The idea behind this project is simple: there is so much happening in lunar exploration, from commercial missions and scientific payloads to lunar landing locations and mission timelines, but finding and connecting all this information can be difficult. I wanted to bring these different aspects together in one accessible platform.

CLPS Explorer allows users to navigate through different sections, including Mission Control, Missions, Payloads, Lunar Map, Timeline, Providers, and Sources. It also features a 3D Selenography Atlas that offers a more visual way to explore the Moon. Instead of going through scattered information, users can explore the lunar exploration campaign through a single interactive experience.

The main benefit of the platform is that it makes complex space-related information easier to access, understand, and explore. It is intended for students, researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts who want to learn more about commercial lunar exploration. My aim is to encourage curiosity about the Moon and help people better understand how commercial partnerships are contributing to future lunar science and exploration.

I developed this project independently using TypeScript, Python, JavaScript, and Shell, along with web development tools and GitHub for version control and deployment. The website combines structured information, interactive sections, and multimedia elements to create an engaging experience.

What makes CLPS Explorer creative is the way it brings several connected parts of lunar exploration into one digital environment. It is not just a page describing missions; it gives users different ways to navigate and understand the bigger picture through maps, timelines, mission information, and visual exploration.

During development, I considered usability, accessibility of information, visual consistency, data accuracy, and how to make the platform useful without overwhelming users. I also worked on ensuring that the website and its multimedia content function correctly when deployed online, not just on my local computer.

As an individual participant, I took responsibility for the concept, development, troubleshooting, and presentation of the project. CLPS Explorer represents my effort to combine technology, research, and creativity to make lunar exploration more understandable and engaging for everyone.
